theater: 萊茵上游防線與日耳曼道路

battle.name: 對日耳曼步路的戰役
battle.theater: 萊茵上游防線與日耳曼道路
battle.brief: 公元二七〇年，奧勒良被軍隊推上皇帝位，萊茵上游的日耳曼聯盟越過河界深入拉埃提與諾里庫姆，邊軍節節退向阿爾卑斯麓。奧勒良沿日耳曼道路北上，在上萊茵擊破阿勒曼尼人的侵掠隊，奪回堡壘與十日之地。卡面的羅馬方陣盾是這道邊防的底子：凸起的長方盾讓步卒彼此咬合，成為能沿路推進的活牆。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 這場戰役是公元二七〇年奧勒良即位後對萊茵上游日耳曼部族的正面作戰，屬於他一生所謂「奧勒良的戰爭」的第一段。羅馬一方是皇帝直接統率的中央軍：駐萊茵各軍團的行省軍、皇帝近衛的達爾馬提亞騎兵，以及從義大利、高盧與多瑙河各駐軍抽調的步兵與弓手。羅馬的指揮體系在此時已經過第三次危機的改動，皇帝在軍中兼具最高統帥與實際戰場指揮者兩重身分，戰爭由一紙軍令和每日軍報驅動；步兵由各軍團的團長分轄縱隊，騎兵則歸步兵指揮官與騎兵指揮官分頭調度，糧秣與軍需由隨軍的軍需官與地方官員在後方城鎮籌措。對面的日耳曼一方不是國家而是部族聯盟：主力是阿勒曼尼人，另有尤廷吉人（早期哥特人的一支）、塞米加利人與拉埃提人的小股部隊隨行；他們的指揮方式是部族大會選出首領，首領自帶一批宣誓效忠的隨從作前鋒與突擊力量，餘下各部按自己的方式列陣作戰。同時代的另外兩個割據政體也在旁邊角力：高盧帝國仍由波斯的摩斯及其繼承者控制不列顛尼亞與西班牙的西部，日耳曼各部與羅馬之間的每一次掠奪都會改變三方實力；更東面的帕米拉王國在芝諾比婭治下於同年底建國，直接抽走了羅馬東方的注意力。羅馬與日耳曼聯盟之間還夾著一段緩衝地帶：從摩根提亞庫姆到奧古斯塔·溫德利科魯姆的日耳曼道路沿線，連同上萊茵、拉埃提與十日之地的堡壘群，構成這場戰役的地理框架；中文把這條通往日耳曼腹地的道路與其沿線防區合稱「日耳曼步路」，這場戰役的名字即由此而來。
countriesEn: This battle was the open Roman campaign against the Germanic tribes of the upper Rhine in the year 270, and it opens the series of wars that Aurelian fought during his short reign. The Roman side was the central field army under the emperor's own command: the legions stationed along the Rhine, the Dalmatian cavalry of the imperial household, and infantry and archers drawn in from Italy, Gaul and the Danube garrisons. The Roman command system had already been reshaped by the crisis of the third century; the emperor was both supreme commander and practical battlefield commander, and the war was run on written orders and daily reports. Infantry was led by the legates of the legions, each responsible for cohorts, while cavalry was split between the commander of the foot and the master of the horse, and supply was organised behind the front by quartermasters and provincial officials working out of the towns. The Germanic side was not a state but a tribal confederation. Its core was the Alemanni, joined by the Juthungi, an early Gothic group, together with the Semigalli and detachments of the Raeti. Their way of command was the assembly of the tribes choosing a war leader, who led a band of sworn companions as his shock troops while the rest fought in the formations of their own choice. Two other powers of the age were pressing on the same front: in the west the Gallic Empire still held Britain and the Iberian coast for Postumus and his successors, and every raid across the Rhine changed the balance between the three; in the east the Palmyrene state founded by Zenobia at the end of the same year drew Roman attention away from the north. Between Rome and the confederation lay the buffer that framed the whole campaign: the road running from Mogontiacum to Augusta Vindelicorum, with the forts of the upper Rhine, Raetia and the Agri Decumates strung along it. Chinese usage calls that road into the interior of Germania, together with the defended sector along it, the Germanic way, and the name of this battle comes from it.
people: 關鍵人物幾乎全落在皇帝與他的對手身上。奧勒良是這場戰爭的中心：他在加里利安努斯與克勞狄烏斯先後猝死、四面都是反叛者的二七〇年被軍隊推上皇位，靠的正是他手上那支紀律嚴密的達爾馬提亞騎兵與他個人的戰場名聲。他不像前任那樣守在行省或羅馬，而是帶著行營大帳沿邊境公路北上；編年史記載他把日耳曼人從遠離河界的地方一路追回萊茵，又在拉埃提境內與他們正面交鋒，並把失守的屯田與堡壘逐段收回。皇帝身邊還有兩類人：一是總攬兵權的軍事總監與被分派出去的步兵指揮官，他們負責把皇帝的戰略意圖變成縱隊的日程、渡河的地點與集結的地區；二是被留在後方、負責維持糧道與城市秩序的官員，羅馬在二七〇年的這場戰爭裡真正吃緊的地方並不是前線，而是糧食從義大利與高盧運抵邊堡的時間表。敵方留下姓名的首領不多，最著名的是拉烏多馬魯斯與英格努斯，這兩位阿勒曼尼首領在次年二七一年打掉了羅馬的第八奧古斯塔軍團；也正因為這件事，羅馬人民在羅馬的競技場上要求皇帝交出日耳曼貴族少年充當軍官團的候補軍官，奧勒良在講詞中為自己辯護。同一時期在西方尚有波斯的摩斯、費爾穆斯與塞普蒂米烏斯各自割據，東方的芝諾比婭則在二七二年秋打開了另一條戰線；皇帝必須在萊茵與幼發拉底之間取捨，這一取捨，最終決定了這場戰役的戰術節奏。
peopleEn: The decisive figures are almost all the emperor and his opponents. Aurelian is the centre of this war: in 270, when Gallienus and Claudius had both died suddenly and revolts were breaking out on every side, he was raised to the throne by the army, and what carried him there was the disciplined Dalmatian cavalry under his own hand and his personal reputation on the field. Unlike his predecessors he did not sit in a province or in Rome; he took the field with the imperial tent and marched north along the frontier road. The chroniclers record that he drove the Germans from far beyond the river back to the Rhine, fought them in open battle inside Raetia, and recovered the lost farms and forts stretch by stretch. Two kinds of men surrounded the emperor. First were the master of the soldiers and the infantry commanders sent out to the front, who turned the emperor's strategic intention into marching schedules for cohorts, crossing points and assembly areas. Second were the officials left behind to keep the supply route and the towns in order, because what really pinched the Roman war effort in 270 was not the front line but the timetable on which grain from Italy and Gaul reached the frontier forts. Very few enemy leaders are named; the best known are Raudomarus and Ingenuus, the Alemannian chiefs who destroyed the Roman Eighth Augusta in the following year, 271. Precisely because of that, the Roman people demanded at the games in Rome that the emperor hand over the sons of the Alemannian nobles to be enrolled as decurions, and Aurelian defended himself in a speech. At the same time Postumus, Firmus and Septimius were holding out in the west, and Zenobia opened a second front in the east in the autumn of 272. The emperor had to choose between the Rhine and the Euphrates, and that choice set the tempo of this campaign.
kits: 卡面是羅馬方陣盾（scutum）：一面半圓筒形、略帶弧度的長方盾，盾面中央凸出鐵或青銅的盾凸，頂緣留著缺口，正好讓重標槍架在盾後。這件東西在公元前一〇〇年已經出現在羅馬的裝備序列裡，是共和國末期那種橢圓形、彎曲的舊式大盾的直系後裔；到了二七〇年，軍團步兵手上拿的是它的成熟形態：半圓筒形、寬約六七十公分、高約一公尺，重量以木胎加鐵件計約在六到十公斤之間。盾的弧度是重點——它把標槍、箭矢與投射武器的力道卸向兩側，也讓相鄰的盾牌能夠互相咬合，列成一道凸出的活牆；羅馬人不是靠盾牌本身的厚度頂住全軍，而是靠盾緣相扣、整面牆按同一節奏前進。在這場戰役裡，這件兵器不是主角，卻是主角們腳下的地面：守在堡壘與村寨土牆後的日耳曼人靠地形與投射武器居高臨下，羅馬人把方陣盾舉過頭頂拼成龜甲陣前進，用金屬的撞擊與盾牆的重量壓開缺口，再由短劍與標槍清場。同時要說清楚的，是它的時代尾聲：分節甲在二六〇年前後就已經退場，前線改用鱗甲、鎖子甲與皮札甲混編；方陣盾的退場也才剛開始，三世紀末到四世紀的《官職表》式編制裡，軍團與輔兵都已改用橢圓形乃至圓形的小盾，方陣盾在羅馬軍的正式序列裡大約還撐了半個世紀。裝備的另一面是馬匹與載具：阿勒曼尼人的衝鋒靠人馬合一的密集隊形，羅馬的騎兵用達爾馬提亞短腿馬與尖頭刺槍，軍需靠馭馬車隊與沿邊境驛站的接力，通信靠邊防公路上的接力騎站，糧草靠多瑙河與萊茵河的水路運到堡壘。營地方面，羅馬野戰營的壕溝、木柵與帳幕仍是一夜紮營的標準形制，敵方則在村寨土牆與林地之間遊走。渡河靠臨時架設的浮橋與淺灘，這是這場戰役裡最要命的技術環節。
kitsEn: The card shows the Roman scutum: a semi-cylindrical, slightly curved rectangular shield with a raised iron or bronze boss in the centre of the face and a notch along the top edge, exactly wide enough for a heavy pilum to be rested behind it. The type was already in the Roman order of battle in 100 BC as the direct descendant of the older curved oval shield of the late Republic; by 270 the legionary foot carried its mature form, semi-cylindrical, about sixty to seventy centimetres wide and roughly a metre tall, weighing something in the range of six to ten kilograms for a wooden body with iron fittings. The curvature is the point: it deflects the force of pila, arrows and missiles to either side, and it lets neighbouring shields lock into one another so that a convex wall can be formed. The Romans did not hold the line by the thickness of any one shield; they held it by rim against rim, with the whole wall advancing to a single rhythm. In this battle the weapon is not the protagonist, but it is the ground the protagonists stand on. The Germans who held the earthworks of villages and the banks of forts fought from above with missiles; the Romans lifted the scuta over their heads into a testudo, put the weight of the wall and the impact of the metal against the breach, and then cleared the ground with the gladius and the pilum. Its late period must be stated too: the segmented armour had already gone out of use around 260, and the front line was mixed scale, mail and leather. The scutum's own retirement had only just begun; in the official lists of the late third and fourth centuries, both legions and auxiliaries are shown with smaller oval and round shields, and the scutum held its place in the Roman order of battle for roughly another half century. The other side of the equipment picture is horses and transport. The Alemannian charge relied on dense formations of men and horses together; Roman cavalry used the short-legged Dalmatian horse and the spatha; logistics ran on mule wagons and on relay between the stations of the frontier road, and despatches on the same roads; grain came to the forts by water on the Danube and the Rhine. On the camping side, the ditch, palisade and tents of the Roman marching camp were still the standard form for a single night's encampment, while the enemy moved between village earthworks and woodland. For the river crossing the Romans relied on temporary pontoon bridges and on fords, and that was the most dangerous technical step of the whole campaign.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術分兩層，羅馬這邊是邊防體系與野戰隊形，日耳曼那邊是遊擊與集結。羅馬在萊茵上游的做法不是一條線上的單純牆，而是一套由遠到近的縱深：最外是河道與對岸的觀察點，往內是烽火台與小堡，再往內是營房式大堡與有圍牆的城鎮，最後才是可以屯兵與修械的軍團駐地；它們之間靠一條沿河的邊防公路串起，公路兩側設里程碑與守望所，消息以接力騎站與烽煙傳遞。日常的巡邏由輔兵騎隊與步兵小隊分擔，真正的戰鬥則在敵人越過河界、深入鄉村之後才爆發，羅馬的戰術是讓騎兵先纏住入侵者、把主力調到合適的位置，再以步兵正面展開。野戰步兵的展開有固定次序：重標槍齊射先行，盾牌抵前、標槍從盾緣缺口伸出，敵人靠近到短兵距離後收起標槍抽出短劍砍殺；密隊形中隊之間保持數十步的間隔，讓後方縱隊能向前填補，兩翼由騎兵掩護，防止敵方繞側。遇到日耳曼人占據的村寨土牆與林地，羅馬人用龜甲陣頂住高處的標槍與石塊前進，再以短劍手與盾兵貼牆清退守軍，弓箭手與擲石手在側翼壓制牆頭。渡河與追擊是兩個最危險的環節：一旦敵人退回對岸，羅馬人必須在窄灘上架浮橋或在淺水處強渡，追擊一旦拉長，隊形就會散；因此編年史提到奧勒良把追擊停在河岸、只把俘獲與戰利品運回，是可以理解的務實。德軍那邊的戰術是另一套邏輯：多數時候他們不打正面會戰，而是以大隊快速掠過鄉村、奪走牲畜與穀物、破壞莊稼，再在羅馬騎兵趕到之前退往林地或沼澤；日耳曼人的首領靠一批宣誓隨從做前鋒突擊，主力則看情況集中在高地上或林邊，等羅馬隊形拉開再以密集的人馬衝擊，衝完即散，不求殲滅。兩套邏輯相遇的結果，是羅馬必須用更重的裝備與更多的時間去換取一次決定性的殲滅，而日耳曼人只要贏一次就能重複再來。羅馬的真正優勢在於補給與工期：只要皇帝肯在邊境住上幾個月，把散落的堡壘修好、把屯糧補滿，敵人下一次再來的時候要付的代價就完全不同。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war work on two levels: on the Roman side a frontier system and a field formation, on the German side harassment and concentration. What Rome had on the upper Rhine was not a single wall but a depth arranged from the outside in: the river and observation posts on the far bank first, then watchtowers and small forts, then barrack forts and walled towns, and last of all the legionary bases where troops could be quartered and arms repaired. These were strung together by a frontier road along the river, with milestones and watch stations on either side and messages carried by mounted relays and by beacon fires. Daily patrolling was the work of auxiliary cavalry and small infantry detachments; the real fighting began only after the enemy had crossed the river and pushed deep into the countryside, and the Roman method was to let the cavalry tie the raiders down, bring the main force to a suitable position, and then deploy the foot in line. The deployment of the infantry followed a fixed sequence: a volley of heavy pila first, shields advanced and the pila thrust out through the notches of the rims, and when the enemy closed to close quarters the shafts were dropped and the gladii drawn. Dense cohorts were kept tens of paces apart so that the rear ranks could move forward to fill the gap, with cavalry covering the flanks against outflanking. Against a village earthwork or a wooded slope held by the Germans, the Romans advanced in testudo under the missiles and stones from above, then worked along the wall with swordsmen and shield troops to clear the defenders, while archers and stone-throwers on the flank kept down whatever was still on the parapet. Crossing the river and pursuing were the two most dangerous steps: once the enemy was back across the water, the Romans had to lay a pontoon bridge on a narrow beach or force a crossing at a ford, and a pursuit that stretched out would break the formation apart. That is why the chroniclers' remark that Aurelian halted the pursuit at the river and brought back only the captives and the booty reads as sound practice. The German logic was the other way round. Most of the time they did not seek a set-piece battle at all: they swept through the villages with large bands, took the cattle and the grain, destroyed the crops, and withdrew into the woods or the marshes before the Roman horse could arrive. Their chiefs led with a band of sworn companions as the shock troops, while the main body massed on high ground or at the edge of the trees and charged in dense order once the Roman line had been stretched, then broke off without seeking to destroy. The result of meeting these two logics is that Rome had to pay in heavier equipment and more time for a single decisive annihilation, while the Germans only had to win once to be able to do it again. Rome's real advantage lay in supply and in time on the ground: if the emperor stayed a few months on the frontier, repaired the scattered forts and refilled the depots, the enemy would have to pay a very different price the next time it came.
data: 能落到紙面上的數字不多，而且多半出自勝方的敘述。兵員方面，羅馬一個軍團的紙面編制在二世紀末是五千五百人上下，到三世紀中葉已降到五千人以內，步兵分三個縱隊，第一縱隊是重裝甲兵與盾牌，第二縱隊為主力，第三縱隊是輕裝；後期每個百人隊多由兩百人編成。騎兵方面，阿拉約五百騎，努梅魯斯兩三百騎；皇帝近衛的達爾馬提亞騎兵約三百到五百騎，數量不大但裝備與訓練最好。輔兵與標槍手、弓手的總數在史料中沒有留下。敵方沒有留下可用的兵力數字，編年史只描述其不可勝計，以及大量的隨軍婦孺與牲口，這類描述不能當作實數。可以引用的具體數字有三個：一是編年史提到奧勒良在日耳曼方向的一役俘獲日耳曼人約兩萬，這是本役最常被引用的戰果數字；二是羅馬競技場事件中，奧勒良提到日耳曼貴族送來三百名少年要求入軍官團，這三百人與被俘的兩萬人同屬這場戰爭的直接後果；三是二七一年第八奧古斯塔軍團全軍覆沒，這支部隊的番號從此中斷，要到更後來才重新出現。疆域與距離方面，日耳曼道路從摩根提亞庫姆到奧古斯塔·溫德利科魯姆約三百公里，上下萊茵與拉埃提的堡壘與烽火台合計數百座；敵軍越過河界後最深處曾抵達多瑙河上游與阿爾卑斯山麓，離原本的防線超過一百五十公里；羅馬的補給線靠多瑙河與萊茵河的水路以及河運與陸運的接力，從義大利運糧到邊堡約需一個多月。時間方面，這場戰役通常被放在二七〇年的夏秋，到二七一年初仍未完全平定，因為要到次年春天羅馬才有餘力從西方調兵回防萊茵。
dataEn: Few numbers survive on paper for this battle, and most of them come from the account of the victor. On strength: the paper strength of a Roman legion was about five and a half thousand men in the late second century, and had fallen below five thousand by the middle of the third; the infantry was in three lines, the first made up of heavily armed men with shields, the second the main body, the third light troops, and by this period the century was normally a double century of two hundred men. For cavalry, an ala numbered about five hundred horse and a numerus two or three hundred; the Dalmatian horse of the imperial household were in the order of three to five hundred, few in number but the best equipped and trained on the field. The total of auxiliaries, javelin-throwers and archers is not recorded anywhere. The enemy left no usable figure for its strength: the chroniclers simply called it beyond counting and described the great numbers of women, children and livestock that came with it, and such descriptions cannot be treated as returns. Three concrete figures can be quoted. First, the chroniclers record that Aurelian took some twenty thousand Germans prisoner in the fighting in the German direction, and that is the most commonly cited result of the battle. Second, in the affair of the Roman games Aurelian mentioned three hundred youths sent by the Alemannian nobility asking to be enrolled as decurions; those three hundred and the twenty thousand captives are both direct consequences of this war. Third, in 271 the Eighth Augusta was destroyed entire, and its numeral was interrupted from that point and only reappeared much later. On territory and distance: the German road from Mogontiacum to Augusta Vindelicorum runs about three hundred kilometres, and the forts and watchtowers of the upper Rhine and Raetia together run to several hundred. After crossing the river the enemy pushed as far as the upper Danube and the foot of the Alps, more than a hundred and fifty kilometres beyond the line they had started from; the Roman supply line ran on the waterways of the Danube and the Rhine and on the relay between water and land, and it took something over a month to move grain from Italy to the frontier forts. On timing, this campaign is usually placed in the summer and autumn of 270, and it was not entirely settled by the beginning of 271, since it was only in the spring of the following year that Rome could again draw troops from the west to hold the Rhine.
cause: 打起來的原因有遠有近。最遠的一層是三世紀的整體崩潰：二五〇年代起，萊茵與多瑙河兩條邊防線同時被日耳曼與薩爾馬提亞各部壓迫，羅馬在萊茵以東的行省相繼淪陷，帝國分裂出高盧帝國，軍團被大量徵發與消耗，邊境守軍密度降到只剩巡邏與報警的程度；到二六〇年代末，高盧帝國的建立與帕米拉王國的坐大，把本已分散的羅馬主力拉成兩條戰線。第二層是直接導火線：二六九年日耳曼聯盟已經打到義大利與羅馬城下，二七〇年春天，趁羅馬帝位交替與西線戰事未平，他們再度越過萊茵侵入上萊茵與拉埃提，一度深入到多瑙河上游與阿爾卑斯麓，焚掠屯田、擄走居民與牲口，堡壘與驛站被一個接一個切斷，邊軍節節退向山區。第三層是奧勒良本人的政治需要：他不是通過選舉或元老院推舉上位的，而是被軍隊在行軍途中推上去的；即位後他必須證明自己的合法性，而最直接、最省事的證明就是在萊茵打贏一仗，把剛被日耳曼人拿走的地盤收回來。同時，羅馬自身也已經改變：加里利安努斯與戴克里先時代推行的軍隊改革，把騎兵與步兵指揮權分開、設立專門的軍事總監、軍團指揮官改為分轄三個縱隊的團長，讓皇帝終於可以帶著一支精銳野戰軍在邊境打決戰，而不是靠各行省分散的守備部隊。對日耳曼人一方，打過來的動機同樣具體：部族聯盟在人口與土地壓力下需要掠奪羅馬的高盧與拉埃提行省來補貼生計，而羅馬邊防一旦收縮，伸進來的手就會更深，於是掠奪與反掠奪的循環就這樣形成。
causeEn: The reasons reach back a long way and forward a short one. The deepest layer is the general breakdown of the third century: from the 250s the Rhine and Danube frontiers were pressed at the same time by Germanic and Sarmatian groups, the Roman provinces east of the Rhine fell away one after another, the empire split with the creation of the Gallic Empire, the legions were repeatedly conscripted and ground down, and the density of the frontier troops fell to little more than patrols and alarms. By the late 260s the existence of the Gallic Empire in the west and of the Palmyrene state in the east pulled an already divided Roman army onto two fronts at once. The second layer is the immediate spark. Germanic confederate war bands had already reached Italy and the walls of Rome in 269; in the spring of 270, taking advantage of the change of emperor and of the unfinished war in the west, they crossed the Rhine again and struck deep into the upper Rhine and Raetia, as far as the upper Danube and the foot of the Alps, burning the farms, carrying off people and cattle, cutting the forts and the relay stations one after another and driving the frontier troops back towards the mountains. The third layer is Aurelian's own political need. He did not reach the throne by election or by the senate but was raised on the march by the army, and once emperor he had to prove his legitimacy; the cheapest and most direct proof available was to win a battle on the Rhine and take back the ground the Germans had just taken. At the same time Rome itself had changed: the military reforms of the age of Gallienus and Diocletian, which split the command of foot and horse, created a separate master of the soldiers and made the legionary legate a commander of three cohorts, allowed the emperor for the first time to take a concentrated field army to the frontier and fight a decisive battle instead of relying on the scattered garrison troops of the provinces. The German side had motives just as concrete: under pressure of population and land the confederation needed the plunder of the Roman provinces of Gaul and Raetia to make up its living, and once the Roman frontier contracted the hand reaching in would reach further, so that the cycle of raid and counter-raid was set going.
impact: 這場戰役的直接後果是邊防線被搶回，而真正的影響要在十年之後才看得清楚。短期看，羅馬重新控制十日之地與上萊茵的堡壘群，日耳曼聯盟被打回河對岸，掠奪的節奏被打斷；短期也看，羅馬為此付出的代價驚人：二七一年第八奧古斯塔軍團全軍覆沒，整個軍團番號消失，皇帝在羅馬城裡被當眾質問，青年與士兵對他的信任被重新算了一次。制度上，這場戰爭把皇帝帶兵打仗這件事固定成常態，奧勒良之後的皇帝都把親自率軍到邊境當成職責的一部分，軍隊的重心也從行省守備轉向集中使用的野戰軍，近衛騎兵被改編成可隨皇帝作戰的部隊，而不再是羅馬城裡的儀仗。中期看，這條邊防線最終撐不住：三世紀末戴克里先在萊茵與多瑙河修築大型要塞、把邊軍與民兵分開編制，試圖用固定的堡壘群與本地的守備軍扛住壓力，結果在四世紀初仍然被越過；也就是說，靠某一位皇帝的一場勝仗把邊界穩住，是不現實的。武器史上的尾聲更值得記：這場戰役大概是方陣盾最後一次大規模成列使用——分節甲早已退場，盾牆仍舊是羅馬步兵的核心；再往後，軍團裝備改為橢圓形與圓形小盾，盾牆的傳統消失，羅馬步兵的樣貌在四世紀完全換了。整個三世紀的意義也在此：羅馬帝國不是被某一場戰役打垮的，而是被一連串守不住的邊界慢慢拖垮，奧勒良的這場勝仗只是讓這個過程延後了十年。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of this battle was the recovery of the frontier, but its real effects only become clear a decade later. In the short term Rome regained the Agri Decumates and the chain of forts on the upper Rhine, the Germanic confederation was driven back across the water and the rhythm of the raids was broken; also in the short term the price Rome paid was severe. In 271 the Eighth Augusta was destroyed entire, the numeral of a legion vanished from the army, the emperor was questioned publicly in the city of Rome, and the trust of the soldiers and the young men in him was counted all over again. Institutionally, the war fixed the emperor's personal command in the field as a normal part of the job: the emperors after Aurelian all treated marching to the frontier in person as part of their duty, the centre of gravity of the army shifted from the provincial garrisons to a concentrated field army, and the household cavalry was reorganised into troops that could fight alongside the emperor instead of serving as parade ornaments in the city of Rome. In the medium term the frontier did not hold: in the late third century Diocletian built large fortresses on the Rhine and the Danube, separated the frontier troops from the local militia, and tried to bear the pressure with a fixed chain of forts and native garrison troops, and the line was still overrun in the early fourth century. In other words, holding a frontier steady with the single victory of a single emperor was never realistic. The epilogue in the history of weapons is worth recording: this battle was probably the last time the scutum was used in massed formation. The segmented armour had long gone, but the shield wall remained the core of the Roman infantry; later the legions went over to smaller oval and round shields, the tradition of the wall was lost, and the face of the Roman infantry was completely different by the fourth century. The meaning of the whole third century lies here as well: the Roman Empire was not destroyed by any single battle, but slowly worn down by a run of frontiers it could not hold, and Aurelian's victory only postponed that process by a decade.
result: 打完了。羅馬在萊茵上游把日耳曼聯盟的侵掠隊擊散，奪回被焚掠的屯田與堡壘，把敵人趕過萊茵，並在沿線重新設卡設站；編年史記下的戰果是俘虜約兩萬，以及被繳獲的牲口與器械。這是一場典型的邊防反擊式的勝利：羅馬沒有摧毀任何國家，沒有一座都城陷落，卻換來一整段重新能用的邊境，以及一批被帶回羅馬的俘虜與牲畜——在饑荒與戰亂接連的年代，這些東西的價值不亞於一次會戰。代價同樣真實：次年第八奧古斯塔軍團在同樣的戰線上被全殲，羅馬的邊軍體系在這一役之後明顯變薄，奧勒良的注意力被高盧帝國與帕米拉王國先後拉走，而萊茵防線在往後的二十多年裡並沒有真正穩住，公元二七七年之後皇帝又得重新收拾同一片邊界。結果的另一層在編年史的措辭裡：羅馬人把這場勝利算在皇帝名下，稱他為「世界的光復者」，日耳曼人則在河對岸記住了一個教訓——越過萊茵是有回報的，羅馬的邊防是可以被打穿的。雙方都從中學到了東西：羅馬學到的是邊防必須用兵，不能只靠一道牆；日耳曼人學到的是必須趁羅馬內部空虛時動手，而不是在羅馬主力回援之後硬碰。至於那面卡面上的羅馬方陣盾，它在這場戰役裡沒有出現在任何一份編年史的文字裡，但羅馬每一列縱隊的推進都靠它咬合：盾緣相扣的那道凸牆，既是這場勝利能成立的原因，也是它最終被淘汰的原因——四世紀之後，羅馬人放棄了這面牆，改用更小、更輕、可以單手持握的盾牌，也就不再需要靠它去對付北方了。
resultEn: The battle was over. On the upper Rhine Rome scattered the raiding bands of the Germanic confederation, took back the farms and forts that had been burned, drove the enemy across the Rhine, and re-established posts and stations along the line. The result recorded by the chroniclers is some twenty thousand prisoners together with captured cattle and equipment. It was a victory of the classic frontier counter-attack type. Rome destroyed no state, no capital city fell, and in exchange it gained a whole stretch of frontier that could be used again, along with a batch of prisoners and animals brought back to Rome; in an age of successive famine and war, such things were worth no less than a pitched battle. The cost was just as real: the following year the Eighth Augusta was annihilated on the same front, the Roman frontier establishment was visibly thinner after this campaign, Aurelian's attention was drawn away in turn by the Gallic Empire and by Palmyra, and the Rhine line was never really settled in the two decades that followed, so that after 277 the emperor had to pick up the same frontier again. A second layer of the result lies in the wording of the chroniclers: the Romans credited the victory to the emperor and called him the restorer of the world, while the Germans on the far bank of the river kept a lesson of their own, that crossing the Rhine paid and that the Roman frontier could be broken. Both sides learned something. Rome learned that a frontier must be held with troops and cannot be left to a wall; the Germans learned that they had to move while Rome was hollow at the centre and not try their strength once the Roman main force came back. As for the scutum on the card, it appears in no chronicler's account of this battle, yet every column of the Roman advance depended on it locking together: the convex wall of rim against rim was both the reason the victory could stand and the reason it was eventually discarded, because after the fourth century the Romans gave up that wall for smaller, lighter shields that could be carried in one hand, and no longer needed it to face the north.
